Costa Rica Construction Materials Sector Hit by Major Cyber Attack

Costa Rica’s construction materials sector is reeling after a large-scale cyber attack crippled the IT systems of several major firms, including Holcim Costa Rica SA. The attack, which began in the early hours of Tuesday, is believed to be ransomware in nature and has disrupted supply chains, order processing, and plant operations across the country.

According to industry sources, the attackers gained access to internal networks and encrypted critical data, demanding a ransom in cryptocurrency for decryption keys. As a result, affected companies are experiencing delays in cement deliveries and are unable to process new orders, causing concern among contractors and project managers.

Holcim Costa Rica SA confirmed in a statement, “We have experienced a significant disruption to our digital infrastructure. Our teams are working with cybersecurity experts to contain and resolve the incident. Production at our main plant is temporarily impacted.”

Other firms in the sector, such as Grupo Materiales Tico, have also reported operational difficulties. “Right now, we cannot access our inventory systems or confirm delivery schedules,” said an executive at Grupo Materiales Tico, who requested anonymity.

The Costa Rican Chamber of Construction Materials Manufacturers issued a call for urgent government support. “This event exposes the vulnerability of our industry’s digital infrastructure,” said Chamber President Laura Jiménez. “Swift action is needed to restore operations and safeguard sensitive data.”

Analysts warn that if the disruption continues, ongoing construction projects could face significant delays and cost overruns. “With key suppliers offline, contractors may face shortages of essential materials in the coming days,” noted local supply chain consultant Mauricio Obando.

At press time, there was no official word on when systems would be fully restored, and investigations into the source of the attack are ongoing.
